title: Support S4 objects
description:
## Preserve the S4 object bit in the shared memory layouts

Before this change, `share()` silently dropped the S4 object bit. A shared S4 vector kept its class attribute, but `isS4()` returned `FALSE`, and S4 method dispatch did not work.

This change stores the bit in the layouts and restores it on open:

- The MORH, MORS, and MORL headers have a new flags word at byte 32.
- A MORL directory entry flags an S4 leaf in bit 30 of `sexptype`.
- The open path sets the bit with `Rf_asS4()` after it restores the attributes. A read never consults a class definition.
- The embedder layout oracle no longer rejects S4 objects.

Not changed: S4 objects without a data part and S4 pairlists are returned unchanged and stay unshared.

Slots are serialised with the attributes. A slot that holds a non-vector object, for example an environment, is restored as a copy.

title: Fix three correctness bugs: corrupt-region crashes, fork safety, string serialization
description:
## Summary

This PR fixes three independent bugs found in a code review, one commit per fix.

**1. Corrupted shared memory regions could crash R.** `map_shared()` checked a region's magic bytes and directory offsets, but never checked that claimed vector and string lengths fit inside the mapped region. A corrupt region with an inflated length field made R read out of bounds and segfault. All header and directory fields are now validated against the mapped size, so corrupt input always produces a clean R error.

**2. A forked child could destroy its parent's live regions.** With `parallel::mclapply` (or any `fork()`), if the child garbage-collected an inherited shared object, the child's finalizer would unlink the parent's region — existing readers kept working, but no new process could map it. The region now records its creator's PID and only that process may unlink it. Benchmarked at 20k share+finalize cycles: no measurable performance cost.

**3. A shared string could be mistaken for its own identifier.** Shared objects serialize compactly as their shared-memory name, but a materialized character vector was also serialized as a plain string — so a length-1 shared string whose *content* looked like a name (e.g. a stored `shared_name()` value) would unserialize to the wrong object, or fail with "region not found". Materialized string states now use a wrapped form that can never be confused with an identifier. The compact identifier form is unchanged.

## Testing

- 15 new regression tests: 12 corruption cases, 2 wire-form cases, 1 fork test.
- Both segfault repros and the fork repro verified fixed on macOS; corruption tests run on Linux CI.
- Full suite: 390 pass, 0 fail.

title: Start region name counters at random value
description:
A process that reuses a crashed process's PID would regenerate identical region names (`mori_<pid>_0`, `1`, …) and collide with the orphans left behind, failing `share()` with `MORI_EEXIST` until pruned. Seeding the per-process counter at a random start makes PID reuse alone insufficient to collide — it now additionally requires a ~2^-32 counter overlap.

Closes #50.

description: Closes #41.

title: Cover mori_err_classify with an oversized-region test
description:
`mori_err_classify` (errno → portable failure category) had no test coverage.

Sharing a region too large to back exercises it on the live create-failure path: `1:1e15` is a compact ALTREP seq (O(1) memory), so `share()` requests a ~7 PB region the OS rejects, without the test ever allocating it.

The mapped category is platform-specific (ENOMEM on macOS, ENOSPC on Linux's size-capped tmpfs), so the test asserts only the size envelope.

title: Remove redundant MADV_WILLNEED on macOS shm paths
description:
On macOS, both the create and consumer mmap paths issued `madvise(addr, size, MADV_WILLNEED)`, which eagerly installs PTEs across the whole region.

On the consumer path this contradicts the design: `MAP_POPULATE` is deliberately omitted there so list elements fault in lazily (a worker reading 1 of N elements shouldn't prefault the rest), and `MADV_WILLNEED` reintroduced exactly that eager prefaulting.

On the create path the region is written in full before use, so the pages fault in on demand regardless — the advise was a redundant pass plus a syscall.

title: Remove redundant `MADV_WILLNEED` on macOS shm paths
description: Target #43 on main.

title: Error when a region name already exists instead of retrying
description:
`share()` names each region `mori_<pid>_<counter>` and creates it with `O_EXCL`, so it never reuses or mutates an existing region. The only way that create collides is PID reuse: a process inherits a PID whose previous owner died uncleanly and left an orphan. That orphan carries the *current* process's own PID, so the current process reads its PID as alive and cannot reap it — `prune_shared()` clears such orphans, but only while the PID is free, before reuse.

So retrying past the orphan papered over a state that pruning is meant to prevent. `share()` now makes a single attempt and surfaces the collision as an error carrying the requested size and a hint to prune before a PID is reused.

Also shortens the internal error enum to errno-style: `MORI_ENOSPC`, `MORI_ENOMEM`, `MORI_EEXIST`, `MORI_EOTHER`.

title: Unify and align examples across share API functions
description: Align the runnable examples across `share()`, `map_shared()`, `shared_name()`, and `is_shared()` so they share the same `1:100` root object and `list(a = 1:3, b = letters)` list case, and demonstrate the bracketed sub-object path form.

title: Replace `unlink_shared()` with `prune_shared()`
description:
Closes #25.

Adds `prune_shared()` to clean up shared memory regions left behind when a process is killed before it can clean up — a crash, `SIGKILL`, or the OOM killer — the scenario reported in #25 (orphaned `mori_*` regions accumulating in `/dev/shm`).

## Behaviour
- Takes no arguments: removes every region whose creating process is no longer running.
- **Conservative**: a region is removed only if the PID encoded in its name is dead, so regions still in use by a live process are never touched. Removing a region unlinks only its name; processes that have already mapped it keep reading until they release it.
- Cross-platform: enumerates `/dev/shm` on Linux and mori's per-user registry on macOS; a no-op on Windows, where mappings cannot be orphaned.

description: Bump versions to latest.

title: Reap macOS orphans via a per-process log, not per-region markers
description:
## macOS orphan reaping

- Replace per-region markers with **one append-only log per process** (`<TMPDIR>/mori/mori_<pid>`)
  - **Why (efficiency):** one `write()` per `share()` (~1 µs) instead of creating a file per region (~40 µs on APFS — the cost is inode allocation + journaling, which neither path caching nor a cached dir fd avoids)
  - Single-writer per process ⇒ no locking; the only reader is a reaper of a *dead* PID, which by definition has no concurrent writer
- `mori_shm_os_unlink` is now pure `shm_unlink`; the registry is decoupled and driven by:
  - `mori_log_append` — in `mori_shm_create`, before the region is observable
  - `mori_log_release` — host finalizer / create-fail; prunes log + dir once the process's live-region count returns to zero
- Reaper reads each dead-PID log, unlinks the regions it names, then removes the log

## Docs

- Trim CLAUDE.md (~24 lines)
  - Drop generic R-package dev commands and the step-by-step parser walkthrough
  - De-duplicate the macOS registry description (now lives only in Platform Notes)

title: Create macOS marker before SHM region is observable
description:
Follow-up to #33.

Moves `mori_marker_create()` to immediately after the `shm_open()` retry loop succeeds, before `ftruncate`/`mmap`. The marker now exists from the moment the region's name is committed, so a crash mid-create can leave at worst a benign stale marker (self-healed by reaping) rather than a region with no marker (an unreapable leak). The teardown order in `mori_shm_os_unlink` (region then marker) already had this property; this makes create symmetric.

Post-`shm_open` failure exits already route through `mori_create_fail` → `mori_shm_os_unlink` → `mori_marker_remove`, so the marker is cleaned up on a failed `ftruncate`/`mmap` with no extra code.

title: Make `test-coverage` resilient to transient Codecov upload failures
description:
`test-coverage` was failing despite passing package tests because the Codecov upload step hard-failed on external CLI/GPG verification errors. This change keeps coverage generation in place while preventing third-party upload instability from failing the workflow.

- **Root cause**
  - `codecov/codecov-action@v5` exited non-zero when Codecov signature verification failed (`gpg: ... No public key`), causing the whole job to fail.

- **Workflow adjustment**
  - Updated `.github/workflows/test-coverage.yaml` to make Codecov upload non-blocking by setting `fail_ci_if_error: false`.
  - Kept existing coverage artifact and upload configuration unchanged.

- **Relevant diff**
  ```yaml
  - fail_ci_if_error: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
  + fail_ci_if_error: false
  ```

title: Support `unlink_shared()` reaping on macOS
description:
Closes #25.

Extends `unlink_shared()` reaping (no argument) to macOS, bringing it to parity with Linux.

- macOS POSIX shared memory has no enumerable namespace — a dead creator's region is invisible to `ipcs`/`lsof` yet still holds memory — so reaping can't find orphans the way Linux does by scanning `/dev/shm`.
- mori now keeps its own registry: one empty marker file per region under a per-user dir (`<TMPDIR>/mori`), created with the region and removed with it in lockstep.
- `mori_shm_reap` scans that directory on macOS exactly as it scans `/dev/shm` on Linux, unlinking any region whose embedded creator PID is dead.
- All marker ops are best-effort — a failure forfeits only reapability, never the region.

By-name removal already worked on macOS; this only adds the reap (orphan-cleanup) form.
Windows and other POSIX are unchanged (no reap).

title: Add tests for string materialization and corruption guards
description:
Closes coverage gaps surfaced by `covr::package_coverage()` (89.66% → higher on Linux), adding tests for behaviour that was previously unexercised.

## String COW materialization via `DATAPTR`
`order()` on a shared string ALTREP demands a contiguous `STRING_PTR`, forcing `mori_string_Dataptr` to materialize the vector into a private copy (`data2`); subsequent `length()`/`[[` then read through the materialized-copy branches. The existing `make.unique`/`duplicated`/assignment tests went through the `Duplicate` method instead, so this path (`altrep.c` `mori_string_Dataptr` + the `data2` branches of `Length`/`Elt`) was never hit.

## Corruption guards (Linux-only)
New `test-corruption.R` hands `map_shared()` regions with a valid mori name but malformed contents, asserting it errors rather than reading garbage. Each crafts a region as a file in `/dev/shm`, so — like the existing `/dev/shm` tests in `test-create.R` — they skip on non-Linux. They cover:

| Trigger | Guard (`altrep.c`) |
|---------|--------------------|
| unknown magic number | `mori_dispatch_by_magic` (1086–1087) |
| truncated MORL header (< 24 bytes) | `mori_make_view_extptr` (533) |
| out-of-range element count | `mori_make_view_extptr` (548) |
| element directory offset OOB | `mori_unwrap_element` (467) |
| element attrs exceed data | `mori_unwrap_element` (469) |
| nested child with bad magic | `mori_make_view_extptr` (538) |
| path-form intermediate OOB | `mori_open_path_c` (1329) |

## Verification
Full suite green on macOS: 383 passed, 13 skipped (7 new corruption guards + pre-existing Linux-only), 0 failed. The corruption guards' assertions are correct by construction (byte layout from the `mori_elem` struct / SHM Region Layouts, error strings taken verbatim from the C source) but the Linux branch was not executed locally — macOS has no `/dev/shm` — so they'll first run on Linux CI.

title: Improve cross-platform error messages on `share()` creation failure
description:
Closes #29.

`share()` now reports the requested size and an actionable platform-specific hint on a shared-memory creation failure, instead of a generic message.

title: Add `unlink_shared()`
description:
Closes #25.

Adds `unlink_shared()` to remove shared memory regions, plus crash-resilience for region creation.

- `unlink_shared(name)` removes regions by name (from `shared_name()`); sub-object paths resolve to their underlying region, non-mori names are ignored.
- `unlink_shared()` (no args) reaps orphans whose creating process is dead — the addresses the docker/SIGKILL leftover case in the issue. Linux only (enumerates `/dev/shm`); macOS supports removal by name; Windows mappings are refcounted and can't be orphaned, so both are no-ops.
- `share()` now retries on a name collision, so a PID reused after an unclean exit can't clash with an orphan left by the dead process.

Returns the names actually removed (invisibly), or `NULL` if nothing was removed.

title: Change return value of invalid input to `shared_name()`
description:
From `""` to `NULL`.

As the consumer of `shared_name()` i.e. a `map_shared()` call is typically in another process, we want to 'fail fast' here and so returning NULL facilitates handling at the point of failure rather than downstream at the `map_shared()` site.

It allows for idiomatic language such as `nm <- shared_name(x) %||% stop("not a shared object")`.

title: Round-trippable shared_name() for sub-objects
description:
Closes #13.

## What's new

`shared_name()` and `map_shared()` now round-trip for any shared object, not just whole roots.

Previously, `shared_name(sub)` returned the parent SHM region's name — useful as a diagnostic, but you couldn't feed it back to `map_shared()` to recover `sub`. The only way to round-trip a sub-object was through `serialize()` / `mirai`, which used a separate internal code path.

Now there's a single round-trippable identifier. Sub-object identifiers carry a 1-based bracketed index path, and `map_shared()` accepts either form:

```r
x <- share(list(a = 1:5, b = list(c = letters)))

shared_name(x)                            # "/mori_abc_1"
shared_name(x[["b"]][["c"]])              # "/mori_abc_1[2,1]"

identical(map_shared(shared_name(x[["b"]])), x[["b"]])  # TRUE
```

ALTREP serialization emits the same wire form, so sub-objects flow transparently through `serialize()` and `mirai` with no special handling.

## Breaking change

The wire format for serialized sub-list and element ALTREPs is now a single identifier string instead of `list(name, int_path)`. Persisted blobs from earlier versions that contain serialized sub-objects won't deserialize. Root-only blobs are unaffected — the SHM-name format itself is unchanged.

## Performance and internals

While we were here, a handful of follow-ups landed:

* Cheaper path-form `map_shared()`. Intermediate steps now use bare keeper-chain extptrs (no ALTLIST wrapper, no attribute restoration), since they're never observed from R. Only the leaf gets a full ALTREP. Deep paths drop a `R_new_altrep` call and an attribute deserialize per step.

* Single-pass identifier formatting. `mori_format_chain` fills its path buffer back-to-front during the keeper-chain walk, dropping a second array plus the reverse copy.

* Free list-cache initialisation. The lazy `Elt` cache for shared ALTLISTs uses `R_NilValue` as its "uncached" sentinel instead of an installed symbol. Fresh `VECSXP`s are naturally `R_NilValue`-filled, so cache init is zero work — formerly an O(n) write loop. NIL-valued elements aren't cached (they're singletons; re-extraction returns the same `R_NilValue`), so identity stays stable for free.

* Cached `shm->name` length. `name_len` is set at create/open time, sparing a `strlen` per `shared_name()` / `Serialized_state()`.

* Tighter struct. `MORI_NAME_MAX` shrunk from 48 to 30 — the smallest value that fits the cross-platform worst case (Windows: `Local\\mori_<8hex>_<8hex>` + NUL = 29) and lands `name_len` in `mori_shm`'s natural tail padding. `mori_shm` drops from 72 → 48 bytes (POSIX) and 80 → 56 bytes (Windows).

* Tighter parser bound. The prefix-scan inner loop now caps at `MORI_NAME_MAX`, matching what's documented.

title: Reserve pages on Linux via posix_fallocate; drop MAP_POPULATE on consumer
description:
Two related changes in `shm.c`, prompted by #14 (Bus error when a too-small `/dev/shm` can't back the region).

Host: `posix_fallocate` after `ftruncate` on Linux. Forces tmpfs to commit pages upfront, so a too-small `/dev/shm` (Docker default 64 MB) fails with a clean R error pointing at `--shm-size` instead of SIGBUS-ing the writer mid-serialize. No extra work — `MAP_POPULATE` would have allocated the same pages on the next line.

Consumer: drop `MAP_POPULATE`. Pages already exist by the time a consumer opens the region, so populating only did eager PTE install across the whole VMA — which defeats lazy access (a worker reading 1 of 10 list elements would prefault the other 9). Lazy-fault on first touch now, matching macOS. The per-platform `madvise` hints are unchanged.

Small API knock-on: `mori_shm_create_heap` now returns `int` with an out-param, so the three call sites can tell out-of-space from generic failure and surface the right message.

Closes #14.

title: `shared_name()` returns root SHM name for sub-lists and elements
description:
Closes #11.

Previously `shared_name(x)` returned `""` whenever `x` was a sub-list or element extracted from a shared list, even though `is_shared(x)` returned `TRUE`. This flips that: `shared_name()` now walks the keeper chain to the SHM terminus and returns the root region's name for any shared ALTREP. Only non-shared inputs still return `""`.

```r
x <- share(list(outer = list(a = 1:5)))
shared_name(x$outer)              # "/mori_..." (was "")
shared_name(x$outer$a)            # "/mori_..." (was "")
map_shared(shared_name(x$outer))  # yields the root list
```

Mapping is whole-region either way, so this costs nothing at the OS level and keeps the `share()`/`map_shared()`/`shared_name()` contract coherent without changing return types or `map_shared()`'s signature. The round-trip isn't an identity — it returns the root, not the same sub-list — but the sub-list is reachable from there by indexing.

title: Dedupe SHM wrapping and fix latent double-free in altrep.c
description:
## Summary

- Fix latent double-free in `mori_make_vector`: the unsupported-sexptype
  branch called `free(v)` after registering the finalizer, so later GC
  would free the same pointer again. Moved the type switch above the
  `malloc` and dropped the explicit free.
- Drop the unreachable "unknown magic" branch in `mori_make_result` —
  all three callers write a known magic.
- Extract `mori_make_shm_ptr` helper (heap copy + shm extptr +
  finalizer), used by the three `mori_open_*` functions.
- Extract `mori_dispatch_by_magic` to unify the magic-based class
  dispatch previously duplicated across `mori_make_result` and
  `mori_shm_open_and_wrap`.
- Collapse the five near-identical atomic-vector class registrations
  in `mori_altrep_init` into a `mori_register_vec_class` helper.
- Mark small, direct-call hot helpers `static inline`
  (`mori_shm_eligible`, `mori_is_shm_name`, `mori_restore_attrs`,
  `mori_string_elt_shm`, `mori_make_shm_ptr`).

title: Make share() idempotent on already-shared objects
description:
## Summary
Calling `share()` on an object already backed by shared memory now returns the input unchanged instead of allocating a fresh SHM region.

## Motivation
Previously `mori_create` dispatched purely on `TYPEOF(x)`, so `share(share(x))`, `share(map_shared(nm))`, and re-sharing of sub-list views or extracted element vectors each allocated a new SHM region — doubling memory use and producing a different `shared_name()` on every call.

## Change
In `src/altrep.c` (`mori_create`), short-circuit at the top: if `x` is ALTREP and its `data1` extptr carries `mori_owned_tag`, return `x` as-is. This covers root-shared objects, sub-list views, and element vectors uniformly — all three already live in shared memory via the keeper chain.

## Test plan
- [x] New `share() is idempotent on already-shared objects` in `tests/testthat/test-api.R` — verifies object identity and `shared_name()` stability across atomic / string / list / `map_shared` result / sub-list / element vector
- [x] Full `devtools::test()` suite: 274 / 274 pass

title: Unify ALTREP extptr tag scheme
description:
## Summary

Unifies the ALTREP extptr tag scheme. Previously `data1`'s tag was tri-modal — a CHARSXP holding the SHM name for standalone vec/str, `R_NilValue` for elements, `mori_view_tag` for lists — which required post-hoc tag mutation in the open paths and stored the SHM name in two unrelated places.

Now every mori extptr carries one of three symbol tags:

| Tag | Addr | Finalizer | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mori_shm_tag` | `mori_shm *` | `mori_shm_finalizer` (munmap) | SHM mapping extptr |
| `mori_host_tag` | `mori_shm *` | `mori_host_finalizer` (unlink/CloseHandle) | host-only outer extptr |
| `mori_owned_tag` | `mori_list_view *` / `mori_vec *` / `mori_str *` | `mori_owned_finalizer` | every ALTREP's `data1` extptr |

Addr type for `data1` is dispatched from `TYPEOF(x)`. Standalone-vs-element is now carried solely in each struct's `index` field. The SHM name lives only at `shm->name`.

Effects:

- `is_shared()` is a single tag comparison.
- `shared_name()` is `data1.prot → shm->name`, gated on `prot` being `shm_tag` (elements and sub-lists return `""`).
- `mori_build_path` walks only owned-tag hops; casts are safe by construction (vec/str extptrs are only ever leaves). Dead reachability guards are removed; the sole `R_NilValue` return is `MORI_MAX_PATH` (64) overflow.
- `Serialized_state` hooks drop the obsolete CHARSXP branch and unreachable defensive checks.
- `mori_vec_finalizer` → `mori_owned_finalizer` (matches the tag it releases).

No wire-format, API, or struct-layout change. COW behaviour untouched. `CLAUDE.md` is updated and `test-api.R` gains six cases pinning the single-tag invariant across ALTREP kinds on host + consumer sides, sub-list `shared_name() == ""`, and COW preservation.

title: Zero-copy nested lists via inline MORL regions
description:
Closes #1.

## Zero-copy nested lists

Previously, a shared list whose elements were themselves lists (including data frames with list-columns, lists of data frames, or any deeper nesting) round-tripped the inner lists as **serialized bytes** inside the parent SHM. Reading a sub-list materialized it as a plain R list — no SHM backing, no cross-process sharing, not even `is_shared() == TRUE`.

After this PR, every level of nesting is zero-copy. A list-of-lists-of-data-frames is one SHM region, and every level is an ALTLIST on the consumer.

### What changes for users

```r
x <- share(list(outer = list(a = 1:100, df = data.frame(v = 1:10))))
y <- map_shared(shared_name(x))

is_shared(y$outer)        # TRUE  (was: FALSE)
is_shared(y$outer$a)      # TRUE  (was: FALSE — it was a plain integer vector)
is_shared(y$outer$df)     # TRUE  (was: FALSE)
shared_name(y$outer)      # ""   — sub-lists have no standalone name
shared_name(y)            # "/mori_..." — only the root has one
```

Sending a *sub-list* or a nested column through `mirai` (or any serializer) now produces the same ~30-byte `(name, path)` reference that top-level shared objects already used — no bulk re-serialization, no new SHM.

### On-disk format

A nested VECSXP element is written inline as a **complete child MORL region** at its `data_offset` — same header / directory / attrs layout the root already used, just recursively. The parent's directory entry uses `sexptype == VECSXP` and its `attrs_size` is always 0 (child attrs live inside the child region).

Old blobs with no nesting remain readable: a length-1 integer path on the wire is identical to the previous scalar-int form.

### In-memory model

Consumers now wrap each MORL level in a lightweight `mori_list_view { base, region_size, n_elements, index }` rather than a full `mori_shm`. Sub-list ALTLISTs chain up through the extptr `prot` slot: leaf → parent view(s) → root shm extptr → host extptr. Holding any descendant keeps the root SHM mapped.

Serialization walks that chain: `mori_build_path` collects view indices up to the root, producing `list(root_name, integer_path)`. Unserialization (`mori_open_path`) opens the root SHM and walks the path one MORL level at a time, bounds-checking each child region against its parent. Two extptr tags (`mori_shm_tag`, `mori_view_tag`) disambiguate the addr type so identity helpers stay O(1).

### COW and GC

- `sub[[k]] <- ...` on a shared sub-list duplicates just that sub-list into a plain VECSXP, leaving the parent SHM untouched.
- Keeping any leaf or sub-list alive keeps the root SHM mapped, even after the enclosing ALTLISTs are GC'd.

### Tests

22 new tests in `test-nested.R` + 1 in `test-list.R`. 239 total (was 179). Coverage includes: list-columns, lists of data frames, classed/named/factor sub-lists, empty and NULL sub-lists, pairlist at depth, depth-3 paths through serialize/unserialize, STRSXP leaves in sub-lists, re-serialization of an unserialized leaf, sub-list COW, sub-list-only GC lifetime, `is_shared`/`shared_name` semantics. Integration-tested through a `mirai` daemon round-trip.
